\title{The Shadow Price of Neutrality}
\author{\IEEEauthorblockN{\todo{author}}}
\maketitle

\begin{abstract}
\begin{outline}{Abstract, 0.2 page}
\item Problem: a long/short pod under a platform's neutrality mandate at a fixed \RiskBudgetPct\%/yr risk budget $\rightarrow$ Sec.~\ref{sec:setting}.
\item Approach: duals of the convex program at a root-found $\lambda^*$; three integer sensitivity estimators against certified secant intervals; big-M against perspective formulations $\rightarrow$ Sec.~\ref{sec:approach}.
\item Q1 finding: the liquidity cap, sector bounds and trading costs carry the cost; factor neutrality is nearly free for $\alpha_{\mathrm{mom}}$; at zero, sector and all-style neutrality cost about the same $\rightarrow$ \ELiqMed, \ESectorMed, \SplitTradeMed, \CTwoSectorTight\ against \CTwoStyleTight, \IdealRetMomMin; Figs.~\ref{fig:costcurves}--\ref{fig:alignment}.
\item Q2 finding: the fixed-integer dual is exact when neither the support nor the active set changes within the step (max error \PredOneMax) and lies in $[L,H]$ in \ErrFixedInLH\ of \IOneBindTen\ binding cases; the best estimator depends on the step: at \IOneRobustDate\ ($n=\RobustN$) the fixed-integer dual is better at $\delta=\IOneRobustDeltaPct\%$ (\RobustFixedFive\ against \RobustFixedTen) and the relaxation slopes at \IOneDeltaPct\% (\RobustPerspTen, \RobustBigMTen) $\rightarrow$ Table~\ref{tab:i1}.
\item Q3 finding: two mechanisms. The default-scaling root bound is Gurobi's outer approximation stopping early (\NThreeEOneDef\ of \NThreeN; \NThreeGapDef\ against \NThreeGapMZero\ with a QCP node relaxation); the cone tolerance inflates incumbents (\ConeDefMax). Rescaling the weights removes both; presolve, not the formulation, closes big-M's gap $\rightarrow$ \RootRescBase, \RootDefBase, \PreBigMRootOn\ against \PreBigMRootOff; Fig.~\ref{fig:formulations}.
\end{outline}
\end{abstract}

\section{Introduction}
\label{sec:intro}
\begin{outline}{I, 0.6 page}
\item Motivation and significance: a multi-manager platform imposes neutrality to protect its other books; each constraint costs the pod expected alpha; the dual is the price of that constraint $\rightarrow$ Sec.~\ref{sec:setting}.
\item Related work: fundamental law and transfer coefficient \cite{grinold2000active,clarke2002portfolio}; constraint attribution \cite{stubbs2010constraint}; factor alignment \cite{lee2008risk,ceria2012factor}; realistic shorts \cite{jacobs2005portfolio}; perspective reformulations \cite{frangioni2006perspective,gunluk2010perspective}; integer sensitivity \cite{geoffrion1977parametric,wolsey1981integer}; sparse portfolios \cite{bertsimas2022scalable}; course texts \cite{boyd2004convex,wolsey2020integer}.
\item Questions Q1--Q3 $\rightarrow$ Sec.~\ref{sec:questions}.
\item Contribution: costs at equal risk via duality at $\lambda^*$, with the alignment closed form $\sqrt{1-\varphi}$ $\rightarrow$ A1--A4, Fig.~\ref{fig:alignment}.
\item Contribution: certified secant intervals that test integer sensitivity estimators against solver error $\rightarrow$ A8, Table~\ref{tab:i1}, \WidthMed.
\item Contribution: a support-stability account of when the fixed-integer dual is exact $\rightarrow$ \PredOneMax\ (P1), \PredThreeMed\ (P3).
\item Contribution: the perspective model's two scaling mechanisms kept apart, and weight rescaling as the fix $\rightarrow$ A9, Sec.~\ref{sec:results-q3}, \NThreeEOneDef\ of \NThreeN, \ConeRescMax.
\item Project type: problem formulation, reusing published formulations in a new setting.

\section{Problem Setting}
\label{sec:setting}

% drafted-by-agent
\subsection{Decision problem}
A \emph{pod}, one long/short equity team at a multi-manager platform, receives each month a forecast $\alpha_i$ of every stock's \emph{alpha}, its expected return beyond what its factor exposures explain, and chooses weights $w$ as fractions of assets under management (AUM, \$\AUMBillion B). The platform caps the pod's ex-ante volatility at \RiskBudgetPct\%/yr and imposes a mandate that protects its other books (the other pods' portfolios). A portfolio's \emph{factor exposure} is $y=B\T w$, where $B$ holds each stock's loadings on six factors; its \emph{beta} is $y_{\mathrm{mkt}}$, the exposure to the market factor. \emph{Dollar neutrality} bounds the net weight $|1\T w|$, \emph{beta neutrality} $|y_{\mathrm{mkt}}|$, style neutrality the other five exposures $y_k$, and \emph{sector neutrality} each sector's net weight $|S_j\T w|$, where $S_j$ is the 0/1 indicator of the stocks in GICS sector $j$ (the standard industry classification). \emph{Gross leverage} $1\T(w^++w^-)$ is the long plus the short weight. A stock's \emph{ADV} is its median daily dollar volume over the last \AdvWindow\ trading days, and the \emph{liquidity cap} limits each position to the fraction $\theta$ of ADV: $u_i=\min(u,\theta\,\mathrm{ADV}_i/\mathrm{AUM})$. Shorts pay a \emph{borrow cost} $c$ per month and every trade a one-way \emph{trading cost} $\kappa$ (1~bp $=0.01\%$); the pod starts from cash ($w_0=0$), so the trading cost is $\kappa$ times gross. Table~\ref{tab:mandate} lists the base mandate.

% drafted-by-agent
\subsection{Data and risk model}
Daily adjusted prices and volumes of the current S\&P~500 constituents (\PanelTickers\ tickers, \PanelStart\ to \PanelEnd) come from yfinance, sectors from the constituent list, and the daily Fama--French five factors and momentum from the French data library \cite{fama2015five,french_data_library,yfinance}. A day is valid for a stock if it has a return and a dollar volume of at least \$\ValidDollarVolumeM M; a stock is \emph{eligible} at a date if at least \ValidPct\% of the \RiskWindow\ trading days ending there are valid. At each of the \RiskMonthEnds\ month-ends from \RiskFirst\ to \RiskLast, each eligible stock's daily excess returns over that window are regressed on the six factors. $B$ holds the loadings, $D=\mathrm{diag}(d)$ the residual variances and $F$ the sample factor covariance, both daily values multiplied by \DaysPerMonth\ trading days to monthly, with $d$ floored at its \FloorPct th cross-sectional percentile, so $\Sigma=BFB\T+D\succ0$. The eligible universe has \UnivMin--\UnivMax\ names.

% drafted-by-agent
\subsection{Alphas and alignment}
The momentum score is each stock's return over the \MomLookback\ trading days before the date, skipping the last \MomSkip, so it exists at \DisclosureDates\ of the \RiskMonthEnds\ month-ends (not the first). It is z-scored across the eligible stocks, winsorized at $\pm\WinsorClip$ and re-standardized, and turned into an alpha by the forecasting rule $\alpha_i=\mathrm{IC}\cdot\omega_i z_i$ with information coefficient $\mathrm{IC}=\ICAssumed$ and residual volatility $\omega_i=\sqrt{d_i}$ \cite{grinold2000active}. It is an input signal; no backtest is run. A $D^{-1}$-weighted regression of $\alpha$ on the loadings splits it into a residual $\alpha_\perp=\alpha-B(B\T D^{-1}B)^{-1}B\T D^{-1}\alpha$ and a factor-spanned part $\alpha_\parallel=\alpha-\alpha_\perp$, both rescaled to $\alpha_{\mathrm{mom}}$'s \emph{information ratio} $\sqrt{\alpha\T\Sigma^{-1}\alpha}$ (the best ratio of expected alpha to ex-ante risk). The \emph{alignment share} $\varphi=\alpha_\parallel\T\Sigma^{-1}\alpha_\parallel/\alpha\T\Sigma^{-1}\alpha\in[0,1]$ is the factors' part of it. The \emph{transfer coefficient} $\mathrm{TC}=\alpha\T w/(\sqrt{\alpha\T\Sigma^{-1}\alpha}\sqrt{w\T\Sigma w})$ is the $\Sigma$-metric form of Clarke et al.'s transfer coefficient \cite{clarke2002portfolio}.

% drafted-by-agent
\subsection{The convex problem \prb}
With $w=w^+-w^-$, $w^\pm\ge0$, and $\sigma_m$ the monthly volatility budget,
\begin{equation}
\begin{aligned}
\max\ & \alpha\T w-c\,1\T w^- -\kappa\,1\T(w^++w^-)\\
\text{s.t.}\ & y\T Fy+\textstyle\sum_i d_iw_i^2\le\sigma_m^2,\quad y=B\T w,\\
& |1\T w|\le\varepsilon_{\mathrm{net}},\ |y_{\mathrm{mkt}}|\le\varepsilon_\beta,\ |y_k|\le b_k,\ |S_j\T w|\le s_j,\\
& 1\T(w^++w^-)\le G,\quad w_i^+,w_i^-\le u_i .
\end{aligned}
\label{eq:prb}
\end{equation}
Because $c,\kappa>0$, at most one of $w_i^\pm$ is positive at an optimum. The optimal value $A^*$ is net expected alpha per month. Each row $k$ has a multiplier $\mu_k$, and a mandate parameter $p$ (a bound, $u$ or $\theta$) has the \emph{family dual} $\mu_p=dA^*/dp=\sum_k\mu_k\,\partial r_k/\partial p$ over the rows whose right-hand side $r_k$ moves with $p$ (A5): $\theta$ through every $\theta$-limited cap ($\partial u_i/\partial\theta=\mathrm{ADV}_i/\mathrm{AUM}$), $u$ through every cap equal to $u$, a common sector or all-styles bound through all its rows; each sector and style factor is also a key of its own. The \emph{elasticity} $e_p=\mu_pp/A^*$ is the percent change in alpha per percent change in $p$, and a constraint \emph{binds} if $e_p\ge\BindTol$. The risk row's multiplier is $\lambda^*$: the price of risk at which a mean-variance investor picks the same portfolio (A1). Fixing the risk budget rather than $\lambda$ compares costs at equal risk, so relaxing a constraint cannot buy alpha by levering up.

% drafted-by-agent
\subsection{The integer problem \pmi}
\pmi\ adds a cardinality limit $K$ and a minimum position $\ell=\MinPositionPct\%$, moves the risk row into the objective at $\lambda^*$, and raises the position cap to $u=\MiqpPositionPct\%$:
\begin{equation}
\begin{aligned}
\max\ & \alpha\T w-\lambda^*\big(y\T Fy+\textstyle\sum_i d_iw_i^2\big)\\
& \quad -c\,1\T w^- -\kappa\,1\T(w^++w^-)\\
\text{s.t.}\ & \text{the mandate of \eqref{eq:prb} without the risk row},\\
& \ell z_i^\pm\le w_i^\pm\le u_iz_i^\pm,\ z_i^++z_i^-\le1,\ \textstyle\sum_i(z_i^++z_i^-)\le K,\\
& z^\pm\in\{0,1\}^N .
\end{aligned}
\label{eq:pmi}
\end{equation}
$\lambda^*$ is \prb's multiplier on the same universe at the base mandate with $u=\MiqpPositionPct\%$, held fixed for that date and universe: a Lagrangian relaxation of the risk row, with zero gap in the convex case. The \emph{big-M} formulation keeps $\sum_id_iw_i^2$ with $M=u_i$. The \emph{perspective} formulation replaces it by $\sum_id_is_i$ with rotated cones $w_i^2\le s_i\zeta_i$, $s_i\ge0$, $\zeta_i=z_i^++z_i^-$. The \emph{rescaled perspective} divides every weight, row and bound by $\max_iu_i$ and writes each cone in its own name's bound, $t_i=w_i/u_i$, $s_i'=s_i/u_i^2$, $t_i^2\le s_i'\zeta_i$; its feasible set and objective are unchanged, only the quantities Gurobi's absolute tolerances act on differ (A9). With $\lambda^*$ fixed, \pmi's ex-ante volatility drifts from the budget: median \VolIOneMed\%/yr in I1 (\VolIOneMin--\VolIOneMax, $n=\VolIOneN$), \VolITwoMed\% in I2 (\VolITwoMin--\VolITwoMax, $n=\VolITwoN$) and \VolNOneMed\% in N1 (\VolNOneMin--\VolNOneMax, $n=\VolNOneN$ in each arm, \VolNOneAbove\ above). Q2's slopes are thus slopes of the risk-penalized objective, equal to equal-risk slopes only at the convex base point, where the baseline (\pmi\ with $\ell=0$ and no cardinality row) is \prb\ (envelope theorem; validated below).

% drafted-by-agent
% verify-by-hand
\subsection{Problem classes}
\prb\ is a convex quadratically constrained program (QCQP); its risk row is the second-order cone $\|(L_F\T y,\sqrt d\circ w)\|_2\le\sigma_m$ with $F=L_FL_F\T$. When $\lambda^*>0$ its optimal $w$ is unique: by A1, $w$ also maximizes the mean-variance objective at $\lambda=\lambda^*$ over the mandate, which is strictly concave in $w$ ($\Sigma\succ0$, and the costs are convex and piecewise linear in $w$); the split $w^\pm$ is then unique because $c,\kappa>0$. The big-M \pmi\ is a convex mixed-integer QP (every node relaxation a convex QP); the perspective \pmi\ is a mixed-integer second-order cone program.

% drafted-by-agent
\subsection{Questions}
\label{sec:questions}
\textbf{Q1} (convex): at a fixed risk budget, which mandate constraints bind, what does each cost, and what determines that cost? \textbf{Q2} (integer): once a cardinality limit and a minimum position enter, how well do continuous sensitivity tools (relaxation duals, fixed-integer duals) predict the true marginal cost of a constraint? \textbf{Q3} (formulation and numerics): how do the big-M and perspective formulations compare as the mandate tightens, and how do solver tolerances interact with problem scaling?

% drafted-by-agent
\subsection{Algorithms}
\prb\ is solved as the mean-variance QP $\max\,\alpha\T w-\lambda w\T\Sigma w-\text{costs}$ by Gurobi's dual simplex (tolerances \QPTol; exact active sets and duals), with $\lambda$ found by Brent's root-finding method on $\log\lambda$ so that ex-ante volatility meets the budget to relative \RootRtol; A1 makes this exact. Clarabel's primal--dual interior-point method \cite{goulart2024clarabel} (tolerances \ClarabelTol) solves the cone form of \eqref{eq:prb} as a cross-check, and the perspective relaxation of \eqref{eq:pmi} ($z\in[0,1]$), whose finite differences give its slope. Dual simplex solves the big-M relaxation and the fixed-integer QP (\pmi\ with $z$ fixed at the incumbent). The \emph{plain relaxations} are the $z\in[0,1]$ relaxations solved as continuous problems outside the MIP (big-M by Gurobi's dual simplex, the perspective by Clarabel), so without MIP presolve or root cuts. Gurobi's branch and bound \cite{gurobi2026manual} solves \pmi\ until the relative gap between bound and incumbent is below \emph{MIPGap} or its \emph{Work}, a deterministic effort count in Gurobi's work units, reaches $W^*=\WStar$ (\IOneWorkFactor$W^*$ in I1 and I2): the Work of \WStarSeconds~s at the design pilot's median rate of \WorkRateMed\ units/s, to two significant figures. Its MIQCPMethod parameter (how cones are handled at the nodes) was left at the default, which N3 identifies as outer approximation. The \pmi\ objective is multiplied by $s_{\mathrm{obj}}=\SObj$ to be of order one against the tolerances; values are reported in original units. The incumbent is \emph{polished}: the fixed-integer QP at its $z$ is re-solved at tolerances \PolishTol, giving $V$. N2(b) runs Gurobi's barrier and CVXPY's \cite{diamond2016cvxpy} installed conic solvers, Clarabel and SCS (ECOS is not installed), at default tolerances against Clarabel at \NTwoRefTol.

% drafted-by-agent
% verify-by-hand
\subsection{Analysis}
\textbf{A1 (risk budget and mean-variance).} With multiplier $\lambda$ for the risk row and $\nu$ for the mandate rows, the Lagrangian of \eqref{eq:prb} is $\alpha\T w-\text{costs}-\lambda(w\T\Sigma w-\sigma_m^2)-\nu\T(\text{mandate})$, whose stationarity condition is that of the mean-variance problem at the same $\lambda$. Slater's condition holds ($w=0$ strictly satisfies the risk row; the other rows are affine), so the KKT conditions are necessary and sufficient, and the mean-variance optimum at $\lambda=\lambda^*$ solves \prb: the risk budget is an $\varepsilon$-constraint with multiplier $\lambda^*$.

% drafted-by-agent
% verify-by-hand
\textbf{A2--A3 (equality case).} With only the rows $Aw=0$, no costs and no other rows, and a binding risk row, stationarity gives $w^*=\Sigma^{-1}g/(2\lambda)$ with $g=\alpha-A\T\nu$; $Aw^*=0$ gives $\nu=(A\Sigma^{-1}A\T)^{-1}A\Sigma^{-1}\alpha$; the binding row gives $\lambda=\sqrt{g\T\Sigma^{-1}g}/(2\sigma_m)$ and $A^*=\sigma_m\sqrt{g\T\Sigma^{-1}g}$. Divided by the unconstrained $\sigma_m\sqrt{\alpha\T\Sigma^{-1}\alpha}$, the retained fraction $\sqrt{g\T\Sigma^{-1}g/\alpha\T\Sigma^{-1}\alpha}$ equals TC at $w^*$, and it is at most one by Cauchy--Schwarz in the $\Sigma^{-1}$ metric, since $g$ is the $\Sigma^{-1}$-orthogonal projection of $\alpha$ onto $\{v:A\Sigma^{-1}v=0\}$ along $\mathrm{range}(A\T)$.

% drafted-by-agent
% verify-by-hand
\textbf{A4 (alignment).} By Woodbury, $B\T\Sigma^{-1}=F^{-1}(F^{-1}+B\T D^{-1}B)^{-1}B\T D^{-1}$, so $B\T D^{-1}\alpha_\perp=0$ (the regression residual) gives $B\T\Sigma^{-1}\alpha_\perp=0$ and $\Sigma^{-1}\alpha_\perp=D^{-1}\alpha_\perp$: under the risk budget alone $\alpha_\perp$'s optimum has zero factor exposure, and factor bounds have zero shadow price. With $A=B\T$, $g=\alpha_\perp$: the projection of A2 is unique, and $\alpha_\perp$ satisfies both $B\T\Sigma^{-1}\alpha_\perp=0$ and $\alpha-\alpha_\perp=\alpha_\parallel=B\gamma\in\mathrm{range}(B)$ ($\gamma$ the regression coefficients). The cross term $\alpha_\perp\T\Sigma^{-1}\alpha_\parallel$ vanishes, so $\alpha\T\Sigma^{-1}\alpha=\alpha_\perp\T D^{-1}\alpha_\perp+\alpha_\parallel\T\Sigma^{-1}\alpha_\parallel$, and full factor neutrality retains $\sqrt{1-\varphi}$ of the alpha.

% drafted-by-agent
% verify-by-hand
\textbf{A5 (envelope).} By Slater's condition (A1) strong duality holds. $A^*$ as a function of the right-hand sides is the perturbation function of a convex program, hence concave, and nondecreasing in each bound because loosening it enlarges the feasible set \cite{boyd2004convex}. Wherever the multipliers are unique (for example under LICQ), $dA^*/dr_k=\mu_k$, also across nondegenerate active-set changes, where $\mu_k$ has a kink but $A^*$ does not; by the chain rule a parameter $p$ that moves several right-hand sides has $dA^*/dp=\sum_k\mu_k\,\partial r_k/\partial p$, the family dual of Sec.~II-D.

% drafted-by-agent
% verify-by-hand
\textbf{A6 (perspective tightness).} For $z\in(0,1]$, $s\ge w^2/z\ge w^2$, so in the relaxation the perspective's risk term is at least big-M's and its value at most big-M's. The perspective of a convex function is convex, and the perspective reformulation is the closure of the perspective cuts \cite{frangioni2006perspective,gunluk2010perspective}.

% drafted-by-agent
% verify-by-hand
\textbf{A7 (one-asset toy).} For $\max\,aw-\lambda dw^2$ over $w\in\{0\}\cup[\ell,u]$, $w\le b$, the value is 0 for $b<\ell$ and jumps by $a\ell-\lambda d\ell^2$ at $b=\ell$, which is positive only if $a\ell>\lambda d\ell^2$. Below $\ell$ the true local slope is 0, and so is the fixed-integer dual; the big-M relaxation's slope is $a-2\lambda db$, and the perspective relaxation's (minimizing $s$ over $z\in[w/u,w/\ell]$) is $a-\lambda d\ell$. For $\ell/2<b<\ell$, $a-2\lambda db<a-\lambda d\ell$, so where both slopes are positive big-M's is the closer to 0, although the perspective bound is the tighter. A tighter bound need not give a better slope.

% drafted-by-agent
% verify-by-hand
\textbf{A8 (integer value functions).} The \pmi\ value $U^*(b)$ is the upper envelope, over support patterns, of concave pieces: nondecreasing by feasible-set inclusion, in general neither concave nor continuous. The relaxation dual is the slope of an upper-bounding concave function, the fixed-integer dual the slope of the active piece, and a re-solve gives a secant across pieces. With $V$ the polished value, $\Ub$ Gurobi's final bound and $\Ub_{\mathrm{eff}}=\max(\Ub,V)+\BeffSlack|V|$ (the slack covers Gurobi's tolerances), $V\le U^*\le\Ub_{\mathrm{eff}}$ at each of $b\pm\delta$, which gives the certified interval
\begin{equation}
L=\frac{V_+-\Ub_{\mathrm{eff},-}}{2\delta}\le\frac{U^*_+-U^*_-}{2\delta}\le\frac{\Ub_{\mathrm{eff},+}-V_-}{2\delta}=H,
\end{equation}
with point slope $s=(V_+-V_-)/(2\delta)$. A case is \emph{certified binding} iff $L>0$ (as distinct from \emph{binds}, $e_p\ge\BindTol$, in the convex problems); $H<0$ is impossible at true optima and flags solver error. In I1 and I2 both formulations are solved at every point, $V$ is the larger polished value and $\Ub$ the smaller bound.

% drafted-by-agent
% verify-by-hand
\textbf{A9 (scaling).} An absolute tolerance $\tau$ on a quantity of size $m$ is a relative error $\tau/m$, so rescaling a row or the objective gives an equivalent problem with different effective tolerances. In the perspective cones $w_i^2\le s_i\zeta_i$ a held name has $\ell^2\le s_i\le u_i^2$, so Gurobi's absolute feasibility tolerance \GurobiFeasTol\ is a relative error of up to $\GurobiFeasTol/\ell^2=\ConeTolUnscaled$ on the smallest cones; written in each name's bound it is at most $\GurobiFeasTol(u_i/\ell)^2=\ConeTolRescaled$. This accounts for the incumbents' cone violation, whose objective effect $\lambda^*\sum_id_i\max(0,w_i^2/\zeta_i-s_i)$ is reported relative to $|V|$, and for certified gaps above MIPGap. It does not account for the default-scaling root bound, which N3 traces to Gurobi's outer approximation of the cones stopping before it converges. The two mechanisms are kept apart.

% drafted-by-agent
\subsection{Finite differences and noise}
The perspective relaxation's slope at $b$ is the central difference $\hat s=(R(b+\delta_r)-R(b-\delta_r))/(2\delta_r)$ of its Clarabel values $R$, $\delta_r=\PerspFdStep\,b$; the value is the objective at Clarabel's $(w,\zeta)$ with each $s_i$ set to $w_i^2/\zeta_i$, so every cone holds exactly. A relaxation fails if its residuals exceed \RelaxResidual\ or its duality gap exceeds $\varepsilon=\RelaxGap\max(|R|,|R_{\mathrm{ref}}|)$, $R_{\mathrm{ref}}$ the value at the unperturbed bound, which bounds a difference's noise by $\eta=\varepsilon/\delta_r$. The one-sided slopes $s_+=(-3R_0+4R_1-R_2)/(2\delta_r)$ and $s_-=(3R_0-4R_{-1}+R_{-2})/(2\delta_r)$, $R_j=R(b+j\delta_r)$, are recorded too; $s_+-s_-$ has absolute stencil coefficients summing to 16 over $2\delta_r$, so noise alone moves it by at most $8\eta$, and a case is flagged as a kink if $|s_+-s_-|>\max(\SlopeKinkTol|\hat s|,\SlopeKinkNoise\eta)$. The \emph{gap} of a relaxation at $b$ is $(R-V)/|V|$.

% drafted-by-agent
\subsection{Validation}
\TestsPassed\ passing tests and logged checks, each with a negative control, confirm the analysis: the root-found QP and the Clarabel QCQP agree on $A^*$ to \KFourA\ and on $\lambda^*$ to \KFourLam\ (A1); A2--A3 hold to \KSixA\ and the A4 split to \KFiveSplit; on \KNineToys\ one-asset toys (two fixed and \KTwentyNineCToys\ seeded random ones; \KNinePoints\ grid points) both formulations match A7 to \KNineErr, the \KNineBand\ points within Gurobi's tolerance below $\ell$ excluded and counted; certified intervals contain the exact slope on \KTenToy\ toy and \KTenMip\ small MIQP cases; \pmi\ with $K\ge N$, $\ell=0$ equals \prb\ to \KThirteen. An independent feasibility checker passes every C1 and C2 solution and every polished $V$. The slope method was gated before I1 on the \KTwentyNineCToys\ random toys (\KTwentyNineCMisses\ misses at \KTwentyNineCPoints\ points) and \KTwentyNineCPairs\ objective-scale pairs (\KTwentyNineCPairMisses\ outside tolerance).

\section{Results}
\label{sec:results}

\subsection{Q1: Constraint Costs in the Convex Problem}
\label{sec:results-q1}

% drafted-by-agent
\emph{Setup.} C1 and C2 (Table~\ref{tab:experiments}) at the D12 dates on all eligible names. The criterion is the elasticity $e_p$ from exact duals, validated as derivatives below. Statistics are over the D12 dates for $\alpha_{\mathrm{mom}}$ ($n=\NDTwelve$) unless stated.

% drafted-by-agent
\emph{Which constraints bind.} At base, $A^*$ has median \AMomMedBp\ bp/month (range \AMomMinBp--\AMomMaxBp), a median \RetMomMed\ (\RetMomMin--\RetMomMax) of the unconstrained, costless optimum. The risk budget binds in all but \CSlack\ of the \CNPoints\ base solves, all of them $\alpha_\parallel$. The liquidity cap binds at all \ELiqBind\ dates (median elasticity \ELiqMed), sector bounds at \ESectorBind\ (median \ESectorMed), dollar neutrality at \EDollarBind\ (\EDollarMed), style bounds at \EStyleBind\ and the position cap at \EPosBind; beta and gross bind at none. Fig.~\ref{fig:costcurves} shows the four families that cost anything. At the tightest grid points the pod keeps a median \CTwoLiqTight\ of its alpha at $\theta=\LiqTightPct\%$ (range \CTwoLiqTightMin--\CTwoLiqTightMax), \CTwoSectorTight\ under exact sector neutrality and \CTwoStyleTight\ with every style exposure at zero. The other families are flat: exact dollar neutrality keeps \CTwoDollarTight, exact beta neutrality \CTwoBetaTight, each other style factor alone at zero a median of at least \CTwoSingleStyleTightMin, gross $G=\GrossTight$ \CTwoGrossTight\ and $u=\PosTightPct\%$ \CTwoPosTight.

\begin{figure}[!t]
\centering
\includegraphics[width=\columnwidth]{../figures/fig1_cost_curves.pdf}
\caption{Cost curves (C2): retained alpha $A^*(b)/A^*(\mathrm{off})$, with $A^*(\mathrm{off})$ the value with that family removed, against the bound; all other constraints at base (dotted: base value). Solid: the $\alpha_{\mathrm{mom}}$ median with its interquartile band over the \NDTwelve\ D12 dates; on the factor panels the $\alpha_\perp$ (dashed) and $\alpha_\parallel$ (dash-dotted) medians.}
\label{fig:costcurves}
\end{figure}

% drafted-by-agent
\emph{What determines the cost.} Factor bounds are cheap because $\alpha_{\mathrm{mom}}$ is weakly aligned with the factors: $\varphi$ is \PhiMomMin--\PhiMomMax\ over D12, and under idealized full factor neutrality the retained fraction equals $\sqrt{1-\varphi}$ (A4), at least \IdealRetMomMin\ (Fig.~\ref{fig:alignment}). Numerical and closed-form fractions agree to \IdealRetErr\ over the \IdealFactorN\ mandate-(i) solves, and $A^*$ to \IdealARelErr\ relative over the \IdealNonzeroN\ solves where the closed form is nonzero and to \IdealZeroAbs\ absolute over the \IdealZeroN\ $\alpha_\parallel$ solves where it is zero. $\alpha_\perp$ ($\varphi\le\PhiPerpMax$) loses nothing and $\alpha_\parallel$ ($\varphi=\PhiParMax$) everything. At the base mandate the points lie well below the curve: the cost comes from the caps and the costs. Of the base portfolio's gross expected alpha $\alpha\T w^*$, the pod keeps a median \SplitAMed\ (\SplitAMin--\SplitAMax) as $A^*$, pays \SplitTradeMed\ (\SplitTradeMin--\SplitTradeMax) in trading and \SplitBorrowMed\ (\SplitBorrowMin--\SplitBorrowMax) in borrow.

Filled: idealized full factor neutrality, mandate (i) (three alphas $\times$ \NDTwelve\ dates). Hollow: the base mandate. Both relative to the unconstrained, costless \prb.}

% drafted-by-agent
\emph{Duals as derivatives.} At every binding key and D12 date (\KFifteenN\ checks over \KFifteenKeys\ keys; each sector and style factor is a key beside the families) the dual matches the central difference at $\delta=\EnvStepPct\%$, or $\EnvFineStepPct\%$ at the \KFifteenFlag\ stencils flagged as crossing an active-set change, within \KinkPct\% (largest error \KFifteenMaxErr); along all \KSeventeenSweeps\ C2 sweeps $A^*$ is nondecreasing and concave in the bound (\KSeventeenFail\ failures), as A5 predicts.

\subsection{Q2: Sensitivity under Integrality}
\label{sec:results-q2}

% drafted-by-agent
\emph{Setup.} I1 (Table~\ref{tab:experiments}) perturbs four bounds by $\delta$ (sector and dollar at \BaseSectorPct\%, all styles at \BaseStyle, and the momentum bound tightened to \MomBound): \IOneCases\ cases, \IOneCasesTen\ at $\delta=\IOneDeltaPct\%$. The estimators are the big-M relaxation dual, the perspective relaxation slope and the fixed-integer dual; the \emph{continuous baseline} is \pmi\ with $\ell=0$ and no cardinality row. The criterion is the relative error $|\hat\mu-s|/|s|$ over certified-binding cases, and whether $\hat\mu\in[L,H]$.

% drafted-by-agent
\emph{Certification.} No interval is violated (\KTwentyThreeViol\ of \KTwentyThreePoints\ points) and the formulations' polished values tie at all \VTieIOne. At $\delta=\IOneDeltaPct\%$, \IOneBindTen\ of \IOneCasesTen\ cases are certified binding (sector \IOneBindSector, momentum \IOneBindMom, dollar \IOneBindDollar, all styles \IOneBindStyle); in the others every estimator is zero (the perspective slope to within \NonBindPerspMax). The median relative width $(H-L)/s$ is \WidthMed\ (\WidthMin--\WidthMax, $n=\WidthN$): lying in $[L,H]$ means matching the secant to that width.

% drafted-by-agent
\emph{Estimator errors.} Table~\ref{tab:i1} gives the errors at $\delta=\IOneDeltaPct\%$ ($n=\IOneBindTen$). The perspective slope has the smallest median error, \ErrPerspMed\ (max \ErrPerspMax), then the fixed-integer dual, \ErrFixedMed\ (max \ErrFixedMax), and the big-M dual, \ErrBigMMed\ (max \ErrBigMMax). Only \ErrFixedInLH\ estimates, all fixed-integer duals, lie in $[L,H]$. The baseline row counts the \BaseSecN\ cases where the baseline's own constraint binds ($e\ge\BindTol$): the \IOneBindTen\ certified-binding cases and \BaseOnlyBind\ more. Its dual is within a median \BaseSecMed\ (max \BaseSecMax) of its own secant, so integrality, not the step, causes the errors. The errors depend on $\delta$: at \IOneRobustDate\ ($n=\RobustN$ binding at each step) the medians at $\delta=\IOneRobustDeltaPct\%$ and \IOneDeltaPct\% are \RobustFixedFive\ and \RobustFixedTen\ (fixed-integer), \RobustPerspFive\ and \RobustPerspTen\ (perspective), \RobustBigMFive\ and \RobustBigMTen\ (big-M).

Big-M dual: of the big-M relaxation; perspective: the relaxation's slope. Convex baseline: its dual against its own secant.}
\label{tab:i1}

% drafted-by-agent
\emph{When the fixed-integer dual is exact.} Each case is classed by comparing, at $b-\delta$, $b$ and $b+\delta$, the signed support of $V$'s incumbent and the fixed-integer QP's active set: P1, both unchanged; P2, support unchanged, active set changed; P3, support changed. Of the \SupBind\ certified-binding cases (both steps pooled), \SupPOneTen, \SupPTwoTen\ and \SupPThreeTen\ are P1, P2 and P3 at $\delta=\IOneDeltaPct\%$. With a fixed support and active set the QP solution is affine in $b$, so the value is quadratic and the central secant equals the derivative at $b$: in P1 the fixed-integer error is at most \PredOneMax\ ($n=\PredOneN$; predicted $\le\PredOneTol$), in P2 at most \PredTwoMax\ ($n=\PredTwoN$), and in P3 its median is \PredThreeMed\ ($n=\PredThreeN$). The relaxation slopes fail differently: their error rises with the relaxation's gap at $b$ (Spearman rank correlation \SpearmanPersp\ for the perspective, \SpearmanBigM\ for big-M, $n=\SpearmanN$).

% drafted-by-agent
\emph{Value functions.} I2 sweeps the sector bound, the I1 constraint with the largest median secant (\NearTieSector, against \NearTieMom\ for the momentum bound). The \pmi\ value lies below the baseline value and is not concave: \GridCertA\ of \GridTriplesA\ grid triples at \DIb\ and \GridCertB\ of \GridTriplesB\ at \DIc\ are certified nonconcave, $V(b^{(k-1)})+V(b^{(k+1)})>2\Ub_{\mathrm{eff}}(b^{(k)})$, and the support changes between \GridSupChA\ of \GridPairsA\ and \GridSupChB\ of \GridPairsB\ neighbouring grid points $b^{(k)}$. Fig.~\ref{fig:valuefunctions} shows the slopes. At $\ITwoFracLo b$, $b$ and $\ITwoFracHi b$ ($\delta=\ITwoDeltaPct\%$, $n=\ITwoN$) the median errors are \ITwoBigMMed\ (big-M), \ITwoPerspMed\ (perspective) and \ITwoFixedMed\ (fixed-integer), none in its interval (relative width at most \ITwoWidthMax). The perspective slopes agree at \KTwentyNineBScale$s_{\mathrm{obj}}$ on all \KTwentyNineBN\ gated and \ExtWithin\ of the \ExtN\ other I1 cases, and none of the \PerspRelax\ I1 relaxations failed.

\subsection{Q3: Formulations and Numerics}
\label{sec:results-q3}

% drafted-by-agent
\emph{Setup.} N1 (Table~\ref{tab:experiments}) solves the \NOneCell\ instances per tightness level (loose: styles \LooseStyle, beta \LooseBeta; base; tight: \TightStyle, \TightBeta) with big-M, the perspective at default scaling and the rescaled perspective, at MIPGap \NOneMipGap\ and WorkLimit $W^*$. The criteria are Work and the root gap, (root bound $-$ best known value)$/|$best known value$|$, taken after Gurobi's root cut loop. Default-scaling results are reported as solver behaviour: they describe how Gurobi treats the unscaled cones, not the formulation.

% drafted-by-agent
\emph{Root gaps and effort.} At default presolve (Fig.~\ref{fig:formulations}) the rescaled perspective has the smallest median root gap at loose and base tightness and big-M at tight (rescaled \RootRescLoose, \RootRescBase, \RootRescTight; big-M \RootBigMLoose, \RootBigMBase, \RootBigMTight), and the least median Work at every level (\WorkRescLoose, \WorkRescBase, \WorkRescTight; big-M \WorkBigMLoose, \WorkBigMBase, \WorkBigMTight). The default-scaling perspective is far behind (\RootDefLoose, \RootDefBase, \RootDefTight; Work \WorkDefLoose, \WorkDefBase, \WorkDefTight). No solve at default presolve stopped at the WorkLimit. The plain relaxations order as A6 predicts on every instance (\KTwentyFourViol\ violations; median margin \KTwentyFourMed\ of $|V|$), with median plain gaps \PlainBigMBase\ (big-M) and \PlainPerspBase\ (perspective) at base. Presolve, not the formulation, closes big-M's gap: at $N=\NOneMidN$ ($n=\PreN$ per arm) turning it off raises big-M's median root gap from \PreBigMRootOn\ to \PreBigMRootOff\ (its plain gap is \PrePlainBigM), and \PreBigMCensOff\ of \PreN\ solves stop at the WorkLimit, the others using \PreBigMWorkOffOkMin--\PreBigMWorkOffOkMax\ Work. The rescaled perspective moves only from \PreRescRootOn\ to \PreRescRootOff\ (median Work \PreRescWorkOn\ to \PreRescWorkOff).

\begin{figure}[!t]
\centering
\includegraphics[width=\columnwidth]{../figures/fig5_formulations.pdf}
\caption{N1 root gap after the root cut loop against mandate tightness, default presolve; one marker per instance ($n=\NOneCell$ per cell), medians connected. The default-scaling perspective is solver behaviour. Thin gray lines: the median plain-relaxation gaps.}
\label{fig:formulations}
\end{figure}

% drafted-by-agent
\emph{Two mechanisms.} The default-scaling root bound is not the cone tolerance. N3 (Table~\ref{tab:experiments}) repeats each N1 root at default presolve; the default probe reproduces N1's root bound exactly at \NThreeReproDef\ of \NThreeN\ instances. Forcing outer approximation (MIQCPMethod 1) gives the same bound exactly at \NThreeEOneDef\ of \NThreeN\ (rescaled: \NThreeEOneResc), so that is the method Gurobi chose. A QCP node relaxation (method 0) lowers the median default-scaling root gap from \NThreeGapDef\ to \NThreeGapMZero, near the plain perspective relaxation's \NThreeGapPlain\ (within $\NThreeETwoTol|V|$ at \NThreeETwoWithin\ of \NThreeN), while FeasibilityTol $10^{-9}$ leaves it at \NThreeGapFeas\ (median ratio \NThreeRatioMed; \NThreeCollapsed\ instances collapse). The rescaled arm's gaps under the three methods stay within a factor \NThreeRescSpread\ of each other. N3 was added after the S3 results and the cold read, to test the pilot finding on the \NThreeN\ instances. The incumbent mechanism is the cone tolerance (A9): at default presolve ($n=\ConeN$ per arm) the default-scaling incumbents violate their cones within tolerance with an objective effect of median \ConeDefMed\ and max \ConeDefMax\ of $|V|$, at most \ConeRescMax\ rescaled. The rescaled arm changes both the rows' scale (divided by $\max_iu_i$) and the cones' scale. Every arm's polished value lies within every other arm's $\Ub_{\mathrm{eff}}$ (\KTwentyTwoFail\ failures in \KTwentyTwoPairs\ pairs).

% drafted-by-agent
\emph{Objective scaling.} N2(a) repeats N1's base instances at $N=\NOneMidN$ at $s_{\mathrm{obj}}=\SObjUnit$ and \SObj. At $s_{\mathrm{obj}}=\SObjUnit$ big-M stops at the WorkLimit in \NTwoBigMWLOne\ of \NTwoArmN\ instances (the others use \NTwoBigMWorkOneOkMin--\NTwoBigMWorkOneOkMax\ Work), and the rescaled perspective at \DIb\ with $K=\FalseCertK$ reported a closed gap while its $\Ub_{\mathrm{eff}}$ lay \FalseCertGap$|V|$ below big-M's polished value, a false certificate. At \SObj\ no incumbent exceeds another arm's bound (\NTwoBeatsScaled, against \NTwoBeatsOne), and the default-scaling arm's median certified gap is \NTwoDefGapScaled, above MIPGap \NTwoMipGap: its cone effect reaches \NTwoDefConeMax\ of $|V|$, while the rescaled arm's median gap is \NTwoRescGapScaled. In N2(b) (Table~\ref{tab:n2}) objective scaling cuts the barrier's errors from \BarrierRawA\ to \BarrierScaledA\ in $A^*$ and \BarrierRawDual\ to \BarrierScaledDual\ in the duals; risk-row normalization leaves its $A^*$ identical (\BarrierNormSame\ of \BarrierNormPairs).

\section{Discussion}
\label{sec:discussion}
\begin{outline}{V, 0.8 page; the coverage list of modeling choices, limitations, trade-offs, unexpected behavior and extensions}
\item Modeling choice, fixed risk budget against fixed $\lambda$: costs at equal risk; mean-variance recovered at $\lambda^*$ (A1) $\rightarrow$ \KFourLam.
\item Modeling choice, $\lambda^*$ fixed within (date, $N$) for \pmi: exact only without integers; the MIQP's volatility falls below the budget (I1 median \VolIOneMed\%, all \VolIOneBaseBelow\ of \VolIOneBaseN\ base points below; N1 \VolNOneAbove\ of \VolNOneN\ above), so the Q2 slopes are of the penalized objective $\rightarrow$ Sec.~\ref{sec:setting}, the baseline at \VolBaseIOneAt\ of \VolBaseIOneN\ I1 base points on the budget.
\item Modeling choices: single period with $w_0=0$; the six-factor, \RiskWindow-day risk model with the residual floor; the momentum construction and winsorization; the base mandate values; the \MiqpPositionPct\% cap and $\ell$ in \pmi; costs as assumptions $\rightarrow$ Table~\ref{tab:mandate}.
\item Limitations: the disclosures below.
\item Trade-off, alpha against exposure: the cost curves $\rightarrow$ Fig.~\ref{fig:costcurves}, \CTwoLiqTight, \CTwoSectorTight.
\item Trade-off, formulation strength against per-node cost: tighter at the root, but cone nodes $\rightarrow$ \KTwentyFourMed; median nodes at base \NodesBigMBase\ (big-M), \NodesRescBase\ (rescaled), \NodesDefBase\ (default).
\item Trade-off, tightness against effort $\rightarrow$ Fig.~\ref{fig:formulations}, \WorkBigMTight, \WorkRescTight.
\item Trade-off, tolerance against runtime: MIPGap \IOneMipGap\ (I1) against \NOneMipGap\ (N1); at $s_{\mathrm{obj}}=\SObjUnit$ big-M stops at the WorkLimit in \NTwoBigMWLOne\ of \NTwoArmN\ (others \NTwoBigMWorkOneOkMin--\NTwoBigMWorkOneOkMax\ Work) $\rightarrow$ Sec.~\ref{sec:results-q3}.
\item What each estimator measures (A8), and why the errors depend on $\delta$ $\rightarrow$ \RobustPerspFive\ against \RobustPerspTen\ at \IOneRobustDate; at $\delta=\IOneRobustDeltaPct\%$ the P1 maxima are \ClassPerspPOneFiveMax\ (perspective) and \ClassBigMPOneFiveMax\ (big-M), $n=\ClassPOneFiveN$.
\item Two failure modes: a support change within the step for the fixed-integer dual (P3 \PredThreeMed; P1 \PredOneMax), and relaxation looseness for the relaxation slopes (Spearman \SpearmanPersp, \SpearmanBigM; perspective per class \ClassPerspPOne, \ClassPerspPThree) $\rightarrow$ Sec.~\ref{sec:results-q2}.
\item The I2 near-tie: median secant \NearTieSector\ (sector) against \NearTieMom\ (momentum); under the perspective slope the order flips, \NearTiePerspSector\ against \NearTiePerspMom\ $\rightarrow$ Sec.~\ref{sec:results-q2}.
\item Unexpected: presolve does big-M's root work $\rightarrow$ \PreBigMRootOn\ against \PreBigMRootOff; \PreBigMCensOff\ of \PreN\ stopped at the WorkLimit with presolve off.
\item Unexpected: the default-scaling root bound is outer approximation stopping early, not the cone tolerance $\rightarrow$ \NThreeEOneDef\ of \NThreeN, \NThreeGapMZero, \NThreeRatioMed.
\item Unexpected: the false certificate at $s_{\mathrm{obj}}=\SObjUnit$ $\rightarrow$ \FalseCertGap.
\item Unexpected: the risk-row normalization is absorbed by presolve (supported, not proven) $\rightarrow$ \ProbeSameDefault\ of \ProbeN, \ProbePresolveMax.
\item Unexpected: the hedged legs (in \HedgedRelax\ of \HedgedRelaxN\ perspective relaxations the relaxation splits a name into a long and a short leg to cheapen its cone; \HedgedNames\ name--relaxation pairs, \HedgedDistinct\ distinct names, the prediction holding at \HedgedHolds); per-leg cones as an extension $\rightarrow$ Sec.~\ref{sec:results-q3}.
\item Slope accuracy holds on every I1 case, not only the gated ones $\rightarrow$ \ExtWithin\ of \ExtN.
\item The earlier iteration's lessons in one or two sentences, without numbers: the fixed-risk formulation and the scaling policy.
\item Extensions: platform coordination by exposure prices (decomposition); multi-period rebalancing (MPC); robust alpha (SOCP); a Lagrangian bound for the cardinality row.
\end{outline}

\section{Conclusion}
\label{sec:conclusion}
\begin{outline}{VI, 0.2 page}
\item Q1: neutrality is cheap for a weakly aligned alpha; the liquidity cap, sector bounds and trading costs carry the cost $\rightarrow$ \ELiqMed, \SplitTradeMed, \IdealRetMomMin.
\item Q2: the fixed-integer dual is exact on a stable support and the best estimator depends on the step $\rightarrow$ \PredOneMax, \PredThreeMed, Table~\ref{tab:i1}.
\item Q3: two mechanisms, outer approximation at the root and the cone tolerance at the incumbent; the perspective formulation helps only with its weights rescaled, and objective scaling is still needed $\rightarrow$ \RootRescBase, \RootDefBase, \NThreeEOneDef, \FalseCertGap.
\item Extensions $\rightarrow$ Sec.~\ref{sec:discussion}.
\end{outline}
